note: Grading presets for the marks percentage calculator. Each preset with a source was checked against that official source on verifiedOn. Presets without a source say so in their label.

scales.name: Pakistan: typical BISE bands (older scheme)
scales.note: Typical BISE grading used before the 2026 revision. We could not find these bands on an official board website, so treat them as a reference; your board's result card is the final authority.

scales.name: Pakistan: revised IBCC grading (from 2026 exams)
scales.note: Revised grading formula decided by IBCC and notified by FBISE on 7 October 2025: from the First Annual Examinations 2026 for SSC-I/HSSC-I (Class 9 and 11) and from 2027 for SSC-II/HSSC-II (Class 10 and 12). Below 40% is ungraded and the paper must be re-appeared. Provincial boards announce their own adoption.

source.name: FBISE notification No. RES&ACAD/2543-5775-00075/330, 7 October 2025 (Revised Grading Formula)

scales.name: India: CBSE Class X / XII (pass mark only)
scales.note: CBSE does not use fixed marks bands: it ranks all passed candidates in a subject and gives each successive one-eighth the next grade (A-1, A-2, B-1 ... D-2; E for failed). A percentage alone cannot tell you your CBSE grade. The qualifying mark is 33% in each subject.

source.name: CBSE: Scheme of Examinations and Pass Criteria

scales.name: United States: typical letter grades (school policies vary)
scales.note: A common 90/80/70/60 letter-grade scale. There is no national standard: schools and teachers set their own cut-offs and plus/minus grades, so check your school's policy.
